message.content:
In a standard Texas Hold’em hand, the most hearts a single player can hold is **five**—one from each of the five cards that make up the best hand (two hole cards plus the three community cards that form the hand).  

So, if all five cards that make a player’s best hand happen to be hearts, that player would have the highest possible number of hearts in that hand. There’s no other “ranking” of hearts beyond that; hearts are just one of the four suits and don’t carry any intrinsic value over the others.
